newsitem.title: USA: FTC staff backs Staples-Office Depot merger-source.
newsitem.headline: FTC staff backs Staples-Office Depot merger-source.

text.p: The Federal Trade Commission staff has recommended the commissioners approve a merger of Office Depot and Staples, a source familiar with the staff's views said Wednesday.

The recommendation is in the form of a draft "consent decree" sent to the commissioners. The proposal would permit the restructured $4 billion deal to go through, the source said. Some members of the staff dissented.
"It was a split recommendation," said a person familiar with the views of the staff.
An FTC spokeswoman had no comment, nor did a spokesman for Staples.

The five-member commission voted last month, 4-1, to challenge the proposed merger in Federal District Court. Afterwards, commissioners said they would look at any serious new proposals by Office Depot and Staples.

A few days later, Office Depot and Staples announced an agreement in principle to divest 63 stores in 17 markets to the other player in the field, OfficeMax. All sides said the price was a bargain for OfficeMax at $108.75 million.
In recent days, the five commissioners received a draft of a proposed consent decree from FTC staff, setting out new conditions for the merger.
On Monday, the commissioners set a meeting for this Friday at 10 a.m. (1500 GMT), although the subject of the meeting was not announced.
Together, Office Depot and Staples operate more than 1,000 office superstores in the United States.
